findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true and also has storage_encrypted = false, exposing the MySQL database with its admin credentials to the internet while leaving data at rest unencrypted.
storage_encrypted is set to false, so the catalog database storage and its automated backups are stored in plaintext and can be read if the underlying volumes or snapshots are exposed.

The DB security group allows MySQL (3306) from the entire VPC CIDR. Combined with publicly_accessible = true on the DB, this widens the reachable attack surface for the database to any host in the VPC.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Any compromise of the EC2 instance (e.g. through the web app) immediately yields full control of all S3 data, all EC2 resources and every RDS database in the account.

The DB password (var.password) is embedded in plaintext into the EC2 user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable from instance metadata by any process/user on the instance and is stored unencrypted, leaking the database admin credentials.
The instance is attached to catalog_app_profile, whose role carries the wildcard administrative policy above, turning the web server into a high-value pivot point for full account compromise.

The EC2 instance's security group portal_sg is not defined in this configuration, so its ingress rules (including port 80/22 exposure) cannot be verified here; the app server is publicly reachable by design per the public_dns output, and rule content is unauditable.
